title: Satvik Palak Paneer
subtitle: Pureed spinach cooked in a tomato-cashew base, with paneer, cream and a Kashmiri chili butter tadka.
protein: ~10–12g protein per adult serving — from paneer, spinach and cream

method.title: Blanch and puree the palak
items: Start with 750–900g of bunched palak to get 500g of clean leaves; wash 3–4 times to remove all the sand
Boil {@palak} in a little water with {@sugar} for 5–10 min
Switch off the flame and move it straight into cold water — this stops the cooking and keeps the spinach green
Once cool, puree it; keep aside
Cut {@paneer} into 1-inch cubes; if you like, shallow fry them in {@oil-fry} on medium until golden — raw paneer works too

method.title: Cook the tomato-cashew base
items: In a blender, puree {@tomatoes}, {@ginger} and {@cashews} until completely smooth — no cashew bits
Heat {@ghee} in a pan; add {@cumin}
When the cumin crackles, add {@hing}, {@tej-patta} and {@black-cardamom}
After 30 sec, add the tomato-cashew puree; cook 5 min or until the oil separates
Add {@coriander-powder} and {@salt}; mix well
Add the palak puree {from Step 1} and {@water}; cover, lower the flame and cook 10 min, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch
Stir in {@cream}

method.label: Toddler — pull her portion here (before chili and garam masala)
items: Scoop {=3–4 tbsp} of the creamy palak into a small bowl
Add {@paneer:toddler}, cut small, and {@potato:toddler} — aloo palak paneer for her
Stir and let it sit a minute so the paneer warms through

method.title: Spice, add paneer and finish
items: Add {@green-chili}, {@chili-powder} and {@garam-masala} to the adult pan; mix well
Add {@paneer:main|the remaining paneer}, fried or raw; cover and cook 2 more min, then switch off
Move the palak paneer to a serving dish
In a small pan, melt {@butter}; as soon as it melts, add {@kashmiri-chili} and pour it straight over the palak paneer
Garnish with {@kasuri-methi} and {@fresh-cream}; serve with roti, naan or rice

method.label: Tip
method.text: The green chilies used to be blended into the tomato puree, and the chili powder and garam masala went in before the palak; they now go in after the toddler's portion is pulled, so nothing changes for the adults. Garam masala usually carries black pepper, so it waits too. The cold-water plunge is an extra step, but it's what keeps the palak bright green.
